brief_rationale: The trajectory met the diabetic-foot responsibility chain: it repeatedly triaged infection/ischemia red flags, clarified medication and dressing ambiguity, preserved urgent escalation thresholds, and converted transport/cost barriers into an executable original-hospital wound-care, antibiotic, and vascular follow-up plan. The doctor actively repaired broken links around wound care frequency, culture/antibiotic adjustment, medication reconciliation, and vascular follow-up, and the caregiver confirmed execution. Multiple high-order points were completed with trajectory impact, including feasible access navigation, responsibility-chain repair, bounded closure with lung CT deferred, and integration of vascular/intervention risk. With no serious or minor responsibility-chain error and at least two completed high-order points, the deterministic grade is Perfect.

closure_assessment.explanation: The bounded episode closed after the patient had been seen in the wound/diabetic-foot clinic, antibiotics had been formally changed and pharmacist-checked, next dressing and vascular follow-up were scheduled/retained, and the caregiver demonstrated understanding of red flags and medication boundaries. Residual risks were appropriately bounded: wound healing and blood supply still required in-person follow-up, and acute deterioration would trigger emergency care.
